subject: HelioCloud private deploy: annotated control/data circuitry review
messages:
From: Martin Lowe <mlowe@heliocloud.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC deploy - initial wiring and control/data split (HelioCloud)

Hi Laura / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We skimmed the diagrams on our side and have a couple of follow-ups before we sign off on the network handoff. Our primary goals are: keep control-plane traffic strictly on the management VLAN (no public egress), and ensure data-plane inference traffic has a deterministic egress path with observability hooks.

Two things we'd like to validate:
- Where does the KV cache replication traffic live? Is it strictly on the control VLAN or a dual-homed data path?
- For tenant-to-model egress, can we pin an intermediate proxy that preserves source IP for downstream ACLs (we run several on-prem peering filters).

We're attaching our sketch of the expected BGP adjacencies (ops@heliocloud will drop it into the shared folder). Can someone from your infra team confirm whether the latest reference diagram matches this pattern, or if we should expect a control/data transit overlay?

Appreciate a short readout by Monday if possible.

-Martin
HelioCloud 
ops@heliocloud.com

[Attachment: heliocloud_bgp_sketch.png]

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Martin Lowe <mlowe@heliocloud.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deploy - initial wiring and control/data split (HelioCloud)

Thanks Martin — good notes. Attaching the current Redwood reference diagram (v2) and a flattened control/data circuit map. High level answers below; I'll loop in more detail.

Quick answers:
- KV cache replication: control-plane only. Cache replication and model metadata updates traverse the management VLAN between control-plane services. They never transit tenant ingress fabric unless explicitly proxied for debugging.
- Tenant egress for inference: by default we route model-serving egress through the tenant egress gateway which performs SNAT; however we can optionally terminate through an intermediate proxy (the "preserve-src-proxy" pattern) that preserves source IP using a passthrough forwarding rule. That adds a maintenance burden but is feasible.

Open questions for our side (so we can confirm the exact configuration during handoff):
1) Do you require preserved source IP for all tenants or only a subset?
2) Can you share the ops ACLs that enforce downstream peering filters so we can test acceptance criteria?

Action: Jonas and I will annotate the attached diagrams and send a version with explicit BGP/MSP peering labels and a small runbook for canary traffic.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: vpc_reference_diagram_v2.pdf, control-data-circuit-map.png

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Martin Lowe <mlowe@heliocloud.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deploy - annotated control/data circuit map

Laura — annotated version attached here (also mirrored to the Drive link). A few implementation notes from infra: 

- KV cache (llm-kv) runs on the control VLAN and uses mTLS to reach the control-plane replicas. We recommend tagging control VLAN as QPRI=10 so on-prem network teams can easily prioritize management traffic.
- For preserve-src-proxy: we propose an intermediate envoy layer deployed in the tenant's edge cluster. Envoy will run in transparent mode and forward to the egress gateway; we add a metadata header X-Orig-Source that downstream peering can map to. This avoids SNAT but does require AS path preservation for BGP policies.
- BGP: normal peering on the demarc with iBGP to our edge routers and eBGP to HelioCloud; we include MED tweaks in the diagram to prefer local egress.

Testing plan (high level):
1) Canary 5% traffic through preserve-src-proxy for one tenant.
2) Run synthetic requests that assert source mapping headers at the peered firewall.
3) Validate KV replication under simulated leader failover (control VLAN only).

I'll also call out a small config change: if HelioCloud expects pure source-IP preservation (no headers), we can provide SRv6 encapsulation as a fallback but that increases MTU considerations.

-Jonas

[Attachment: laura_jonas_annotated_circuit_map.pdf]

2) Confirmation whether preserve-src-proxy needs to be global or tenant-scoped. If tenant-scoped, we'll include the config toggle in the provisioning template and add it to the runbook.
